patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hive and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Frame: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hive and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.. Choose Hive only if your buying job matches “Work management platform with free plan (≤10 members) and Teams from $12/user/mo annual — ” rather than Microsoft Project's shape. Choose Microsoft Project only if your buying job matches “Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan ” rather than Hive's shape. Workflow advantage: Hive leans team-collaboration-work; Microsoft Project leans resource-planning, timeline-reporting. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Hive and Microsoft Project share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Hive is Work management platform with free plan (≤10 members) and Teams from $12/user/mo annual — strong monday.com peer.; Microsoft Project is Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Planner Plan 1 from ~$10/user/mo..
- Company-size focus: Hive (micro, small-business, mid-market) vs Microsoft Project (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Hive-leaning team-collaboration-work vs Microsoft Project-leaning resource-planning, timeline-reporting.
- Researched limits: Hive — Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams; Microsoft Project — SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans.

Limitations — Hive: Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams; Free storage (200MB) and AI credits (1k) are tight for active teams; Microsoft Project: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans; Best value assumes Microsoft 365 standardisation.

Poor-fit cases: Hive is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Free and Starter cap members/projects at 10 — growth forces Teams · Microsoft Project is a poor fit when that limitation bites: SKU and licensing complexity across Planner/Project plans · Avoid Hive if you actually need Microsoft Project's motion (Microsoft 365 project / Planner ladder for Gantt, resources and portfolios — Pla)

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
